question: Who should standard precautions apply to in the hospital?

options.A: Individuals showing visible symptoms of disease
options.B: Patients admitted to surgical wards only
options.C: Only patients with confirmed viral infections
options.D: All patients regardless of their diagnosis

explanation: Standard precautions are used for every patient care encounter to prevent exposure, regardless of their diagnosis. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h1)

question: Which body fluid is excluded from standard precautions?

options.A: Cerebrospinal fluid from a lumbar puncture

explanation: Intact skin and sweat do not transmit bloodborne pathogens, so they are excluded unless they contain visible blood. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h1)

question: How long should you rub your hands together when using an alcohol-based hand sanitizer?
explanation: Applying friction for 20 to 30 seconds ensures that all surfaces of the hands are properly sanitized. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h2)

question: A patient has Clostridium difficile colitis. What is the correct hand hygiene method?

options.A: Washing hands thoroughly with soap and water
options.B: Rinsing hands briefly under running tap water
options.C: Applying a rapid-drying alcohol hand sanitizer
options.D: Wiping hands with a dry sterile gauze pad

explanation: Alcohol hand rubs cannot kill bacterial spores, so you must physically wash them away with soap and water. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h2)

question: Which piece of protective gear requires you to perform a user seal check after putting it on?
explanation: A seal check makes sure the N95 fits tightly against your face to block airborne particles. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h3)

question: You are about to flush out a large, infected wound. What PPE should you wear?

options.A: Sterile gloves and an isolation gown only
options.B: Mask, eye protection, gown, and gloves
options.C: Face shield and sterile surgical cap only
options.D: N95 respirator and clean examination gloves

explanation: Wound irrigation causes fluid splashes, so you need full facial and body protection to stay safe. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h3)

question: What is the key safety rule when handling used injection needles?

options.A: Store used needles in kidney dishes at the bedside
options.B: Break the needle off the syringe before disposal
options.C: Always recap needles firmly before walking to the bin
options.D: Never recap needles using a two-handed technique

explanation: Using both hands to recap a needle is a major cause of accidental needle-prick injuries. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h4)

question: A sharps container in the treatment room is three-quarters full. What should you do?

options.A: Close and seal the container for safe disposal
options.B: Transfer half the contents into a smaller empty box
options.C: Leave it open until the end of the current shift
options.D: Press the contents down to create more usable space

explanation: Sharps containers should never be overfilled or compressed; seal and replace them when they reach the fill line. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h4)

question: If you do not have a tissue, where should you cough or sneeze?

options.C: Into the inner bend of the elbow

explanation: Coughing into your elbow stops germs from getting onto your hands, where they can spread to surfaces. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h5)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic coughing constantly and producing thick sputum. What should you do first?

options.A: Draw blood samples for a complete blood count immediately
options.B: Admit the patient directly to the intensive care unit for isolation
options.C: Administer a broad-spectrum oral antibiotic without a doctor's order
options.D: Provide a surgical mask and guide the patient to a separate seating area

explanation: Giving the patient a mask and moving them away from others helps stop the spread of airborne droplets in waiting areas. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h5)

question: Which surface in a patient's room needs to be cleaned and disinfected most often?

options.A: Interior walls away from the bed
options.C: The ceiling tiles above the bed
options.D: The underside of the patient mattress

explanation: High-touch surfaces are handled constantly by patients and staff, making them easy spreaders of germs. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h6)

question: Why is it important to follow the correct contact time when using a hospital disinfectant?

options.A: It ensures the solution dries without leaving water marks
options.B: It guarantees the chemical kills the targeted microorganisms
options.C: It prevents the cleaning cloth from sticking to the surface
options.D: It stops the solution from producing toxic chemical fumes

explanation: Disinfectants need to stay wet on a surface for a specific amount of time to actually destroy germs. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h6)

question: Which type of waste goes into a yellow bin with a biohazard symbol?

options.B: Leftover food scraps from patient trays

explanation: Yellow biohazard bins are meant for items that have body fluids on them. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h7)

question: Why do hospitals sort waste right at the spot where it is generated?

options.A: Reducing the physical weight of bins carried by housekeeping
options.B: Lowering the cost of purchasing heavy-duty plastic liners
options.C: Preventing injury and contamination during handling and disposal
options.D: Ensuring all hospital refuse can be recycled into new plastics

explanation: Sorting waste immediately keeps hazardous materials managed safely and protects waste handlers. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h7)

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do after accidentally getting poked by a used needle?

options.A: Wash the puncture site immediately with soap and water
options.B: Apply a tight tourniquet above the site of injury
options.C: Report to the hospital administration at the end of the shift
options.D: Squeeze the wound hard to force out trapped blood

explanation: Washing the site right away helps lower the amount of germs entering the body before further medical checks. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h8)

question: Why must a nurse report an accidental needle-prick injury right away?

options.A: To prove negligence on the part of the hospital management
options.B: To avoid disciplinary action from the nursing council
options.C: To secure financial compensation for emotional distress
options.D: To allow timely administration of post-exposure prophylaxis

explanation: Preventive medicines work best when started within hours of an exposure incident. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h8)
